verification.acceptance_test: AT1: Open/transfer/close with real child produce no execute frame; lifecycle payload/role abuse rejected. Child survives opening client exit; duplicate open cannot acquire lock; close reaps owned processes. One outstanding gate operation rejects a second submit without dispatch.

AT2: Validate every emitted session/operation record against existing schemas and C12 relational checks; reject at least one wrong-type/forbidden-field record. Concurrent reads see complete JSON; running state precedes dispatch; malformed/mismatched child frames do not forge completion; no development result accepted as acceptance evidence. Resubmit an outstanding operation_id and a completed operation_id with changed payload: require explicit conflict, no second child receipt or effect, and preservation of the original operation/result bytes (or result absence while pending). Hold the original operation with the gate to avoid completion races; release it normally after the pending duplicate probe. A subsequent legitimate fresh-ID mutation/read must succeed, rejecting always-conflict controls.

AT3: Existing F105 claim map contains exactly one runtime_session|tools/test_runtime_session.py row and real stub/suite paths; exercise actual claim-map function against valid mapping and missing/duplicate/missing-suite scratch mutants, preserve other claims and foundation fixtures. Verify the existing fixture harness schedules precisely these nine commands and propagates a targeted suite failure; avoid recursive full-harness invocation from the claim check.
AT4: Case1: owner mutation succeeds; different agent submit and observe are refused as foreign_owner, executed:false, without child receipt or memory change; legitimate owner still reads its value.
AT5: Case2: two detached sessions execute set/get for the same symbol with different values, distinct live child identities and generations; interleaved reads preserve each image and cleanup both.

AT6: Case3: restart same session creates increasing counter/new nonce; old expected generation is rejected before dispatch, including observe; matching current generation succeeds; malformed echoed generation cannot validate startup/response.

AT7: Case8 policy: public CLI refuses review_trial on every exposed action and proposed ownership before endpoint creation/contact, returns error:review_trial and writes no operation record. A trusted harness injecting a well-shaped trial submit directly into the controller receives a supervisor-written rejected/executed:false record without child dispatch. Observe both refusal paths and absence of unauthorized state overwrite; no mechanism-layer isolation or authentication claim.

AT8: Case9: seed a real-shaped scratch run_state circuit entry for a failing step, restart child and submit with unchanged contract/step/attempt; source state bytes remain identical. Lower/reset/missing/changed/malformed counter or mismatched attempt fails before dispatch. Generation replacement never grants new budget.

AT9: Case13: human-to-agent and agent-to-human explicit handover changes owner and increments lease; old holder/old lease requests fail before execution, new holder succeeds. Transfer while busy rejects and preserves outstanding state; transfer never executes code.

interface.cli: python3 tools/runtime_session.py ACTION --root ABSOLUTE_STATE_ROOT --request REQUEST.json; ACTION is open-session, submit-operation, poll-operation, transfer-session, close-session. No shell-eval interface. --help documents usage. Reserved cancel-operation/reattach-session/accept return unsupported without side effects; feature127/020 own those semantics.
interface.responses: Exactly one JSON object on stdout: {ok:boolean, result:object} on success or {ok:false,error:string,result?:object} on failure; a well-shaped rejected submit includes its rejected operation record as result. Exit 0 means successful lifecycle/read or admitted submit, 1 means policy/admission rejection, 64 malformed input/usage, 70 infrastructure failure. Errors never imply operation completion. Submit/poll result is the existing operation record; open/transfer result is the existing session record; close result contains closed:true and session_id only after observed child/supervisor shutdown.
interface.identity: All non-open requests supply session_id, requester, expected_generation and expected_lease_epoch. Submit also requires operation_id, contract_id, step_key, attempt, kind, payload, context and limits as tools/interface.md section6 and existing schemas define. Reject wrong types, missing identity, extra/unrecognized protocol fields and unsafe identifiers (IDs restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-]+, max128). Never interpret a request value as a filesystem traversal or shell command.
interface.open: Request contains session_id, requester, owner, purpose:develop, contract_id, step_key, attempt, run_state_path (absolute). Start only the committed sibling stub using sys.executable; no arbitrary runtime command/config evaluation. Remember run_state_path and governed identity in controller metadata. New session lease=0; reopening a closed/crashed incarnation retains owner/lease and governed identity and requires matching prior generation/lease. Never reopen a live supervisor or silently replace an owner.
interface.policy: Caller identity is declared workflow identity, not authenticated. Agent lifecycle requester must be Orchestrator; agent submit requester must be Generator and exactly match owner; a human requester may operate its explicitly owned session and explicitly transfer/close it. Orchestrator transfer/close remains explicit and requires current generation/lease. Open may nominate a human or Generator owner only. Public CLI denies review_trial in requester/proposed owner before endpoint creation/contact and returns exit1 with error:review_trial, no endpoint and no operation-record write. The supervisor independently denies well-formed trial submits delivered by a trusted test harness directly to its socket; only the supervisor writes that executed:false rejected operation record. Reject purpose:accept and unsupported role/permission combinations.
interface.transfer: Request adds new_owner. Check lifecycle authority and current generation/lease, change owner explicitly and increment lease exactly once; write previous_owner and previous_lease_epoch per schema. Reject transfer while an operation is outstanding, preserving it. Same-owner transfer rejected. New owner must be human or Generator. Old owner and old lease cannot execute after transfer.
interface.poll_close: poll-operation adds operation_id and returns observed durable outcome only to current owner or lifecycle Orchestrator after identity checks; no callbacks or waiting semantics. close-session invokes no project code, terminates/reaps child and supervisor with bounded waiting, records observed termination for an outstanding operation and preserves records/effects. Infrastructure uncertainty stays unknown/busy and exit70, never fabricated success.
interface.storage: ROOT/session_id contains supervisor.lock, control.sock, controller.json (transport/process metadata), runtime_session.json and operations/operation_id.json plus operation_id.result.json for child result frames. Schema records contain only permitted fields; private PID/socket/attempt binding/result values stay outside them. Lifecycle status is read from files, no new status endpoint.
interface.supervisor: One detached supervisor owns the per-session nonblocking exclusive flock for its lifetime and one child. Client exits do not kill it. Unix-domain socket requests use bounded JSON lines; child requests use stdin and child responses fd3. Persisted PID alone never proves identity; only lock ownership plus matching live handshake permits dispatch. Existing live lock rejects second open. Never unlink/recreate a held lock to bypass exclusion.
interface.generation: Under the exclusive lock, durably increment a per-session counter and create secrets.token_hex(16) nonce for each new child incarnation, including failed startup/reconstruction. Child must echo generation in ready handshake and every operation response. Reject stale expected generation/lease before forwarding. Late, malformed, mismatched or unsolicited responses never complete another operation; fail closed and preserve uncertainty.
interface.wire: Controller sends {type:init,generation:{counter,nonce}}; child answers {type:ready,generation}. Only {type:execute,request:SUBMIT_REQUEST,generation} executes stub behavior. Child answers {type:result,operation_id,generation,status:completed,result:JSON_VALUE,image_consistent:true}. No lifecycle message carries executable payload. Default per-line bound 65536 bytes; reject oversize/malformed frames, bound startup/control waits to5s and close to5s; child stdout/stderr are bounded diagnostic files, never protocol or acceptance evidence.
interface.stub: Per-process memory map only, never Python eval/exec. payload.expression is a JSON string with op:set plus name/value, op:get plus name, or op:gate plus absolute release_path in the scratch root. gate waits until the test creates that file; all execute frames, including observe, enter the same lane. Result frames expose get/set result; received operation IDs are appended/flushed to child stdout before execution so tests can distinguish refusal from hidden dispatch. No state/config/source is evaluated during init or lifecycle.
interface.serialization: Single supervisor event loop serializes admission, transfer, record replacement and child responses. At most one outstanding operation; no queue. A second submit returns rejected/session_busy before dispatch. Duplicate operation_id cannot overwrite prior operation/effect; return conflict without executing. Owner/generation/lease/trial/attempt checks occur before any execute frame, including observe. Duplicate-ID admission is checked before busy admission: any reused operation_id returns conflict even while outstanding; a different new ID while busy returns session_busy. Preserve the original operation/result bytes, including result absence while pending.
interface.records: Use same-directory temporary files, flush/fsync and os.replace for each durable JSON record. Persist generation before spawn and running/outstanding state before dispatch; publish terminal operation before clearing outstanding. Crash disagreement fails closed on reopen; never dispatch from ambiguous state. Keep prior operation/result files. Every operation has evidence_class:development; image_consistent reflects observation, not source/heap identity. Only the supervisor writes operation records. Malformed input and upstream CLI trial denials return error receipts without operation records or state mutation. Schema-shaped submits reaching the supervisor and rejected there have executed:false and reason foreign_owner, stale_generation, stale_lease, session_busy, review_trial or attempt_mismatch as applicable; malformed requests are usage errors without invented records.
interface.attempt_guard: Read run_state.circuit_breaker[step_key].attempts on open and every submit; require its integer>=1 to equal request.attempt and session-bound contract_id/step_key/attempt. Missing/malformed/changed counts fail closed before execution. Store the initial binding in controller metadata, preserve it across child restart, and emit previous_* identity when generation changed per schema. Never write run_state, increment/reset counters or infer a fresh governed attempt from a new PID/generation. A newly authorized attempt needs a separately opened session with Root-provided state.

independent_ownership.author: Independent Evaluator authors tools/test_runtime_session.py after both pre-code gates; distinct recorded session identity reviews its bundle. No test implementation exists or is approved by this proposal.
independent_ownership.runner: Exactly the nine commands below select required obligations. Unknown switches/checks/cases/runtimes, missing cases, setup errors or absent proof fail nonzero. --require-sbcl/--require-isolation are fail-closed capability guards, never skip flags; unsupported unimplemented selections fail. Tests use real subprocesses and temporary state/resources, bounded waits and finally-based child/process-group cleanup. Malformed child/late-frame tests may alter the stub only in a disposable scratch candidate with distinct recorded identity, not its committed bytes; no arbitrary executable selection is added to the public CLI. Stub acceptance does not require SBCL or user-namespace isolation; absence of those unrelated local capabilities cannot skip/fail these nine stub commands.
independent_ownership.sealing: Seal test bytes, agreed interface/obligation projection, normative input blob identities and exact exercised source revision. Link immutable Git objects/historical evidence instead of copying repositories. Mutable Root-owned status/budget/history are checked by field ownership and attributed transitions, not whole-file seals.
independent_ownership.red: Evaluator records intended behavioral red before repair with exact assertion/exit/output. Missing CLI/module, syntax/setup failure, timeout from missing setup or unsupported action is not semantic red. If needed, a separately identified minimal API scaffold within this approved scope may be implemented after pre-code approval and test seal; its working transport/setup is independently confirmed before intended-behavior red. Alternatively use narrowly targeted semantic mutants of an executable candidate in scratch, with positive control; neither establishes pristine-base red.
independent_ownership.change_control: Generator never modifies sealed tests. A test defect returns to its independent author and renewed bundle review/seal; preserve old failures. Product changes remain within contract or require both renewed pre-code gates. Exactly one additional Evaluator-originated adversarial QA spot-check accompanies fresh QA.
